Test differences in forecast accuracy between models (Diebold-Mariano)

Source: R/eval-dm.R
mt_dm_test.Rd

Tests whether models of a backtest differ in their expected score with the Diebold-Mariano test (Diebold and Mariano 1995) and the small-sample correction of Harvey, Leybourne and Newbold (1997). It complements mt_score_table(), which shows the mean scores: the test says whether a difference is larger than the variation between forecast origins.

Usage

mt_dm_test(
  backtest,
  ref = NULL,
  metrics = "crps",
  targets = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  alternative = c("two.sided", "less", "greater"),
  varestimator = c("acf", "bartlett")
)

Arguments

backtest

An mt_backtest() or mt_compare() result with at least two models. Models are identified by model, and by "model (prep)" when a model was backtested with several preprocessing pipelines.

ref

Reference model (default: the first model). Every other model is compared with it.

metrics

Scores to compare: "crps", "wis", "ae" (absolute error of the median) and "se" (squared error of the median). CRPS and WIS compare whole predictive distributions; "ae" and "se" the medians only.

targets

Targets to test (default: all in the backtest; see quantities and contrast in mt_backtest()).

by

Optional stratum columns (for example "sex"): the losses per origin and the tests are then computed separately for each of their values.

alternative

"two.sided", "less" (the model has a lower expected score than ref, that is, it is more accurate) or "greater".

varestimator

"acf" (sum of the autocovariances, default) or "bartlett" (Bartlett weights), as in forecast::dm.test().

Value

A data.table with one row per model (other than ref), value of by, target, metric and horizon: model, ref, the by columns, target, metric, horizon (a factor: the horizons, then "all"), n_origins (number of losses tested), lag (largest autocovariance lag used), score and score_ref (mean loss over the origins), mean_diff (score - score_ref; negative when the model is more accurate), statistic (Diebold-Mariano statistic with the correction of Harvey et al.) and p_value.

Details

The test uses one loss per forecast origin, the time index of a rolling-origin backtest. Scores of the cells of one origin and horizon (ages, strata) concern the same test year and are strongly dependent, so they are averaged first:

  • per horizon h: the mean score over the cells of each origin at that horizon gives one loss per origin and model. The differences between the losses of a model and of ref form a series over the origins, tested with the autocovariances up to lag h - 1 (the errors of forecasts h years ahead from consecutive origins build up over overlapping years).

  • overall (horizon = "all"): the mean of these per-horizon losses over all horizons gives one loss per origin, tested with the largest horizon H (lags up to H - 1). Only origins scored at every horizon enter.

Only cells scored for both models enter (the same origin, horizon, stratum, age group, year and target). The statistic, its variance (sum of autocovariances, or Bartlett weights with varestimator = "bartlett"), the correction factor and the t distribution with T - 1 degrees of freedom (T origins) are those of forecast::dm.test(e1, e2, h = h, power = 1) with e1 and e2 the losses per origin (scores are not negative, so the loss is the score itself). With origins spaced s years apart (for example origins = seq(1981, 2001, by = 10)), test years overlap only up to lag ceiling(h / s) - 1, which is used instead; with unequal spacing the smallest gap counts.

With few origins the test has little power: a backtest with 6 origins finds only large and consistent differences. When the number of origins T is not larger than the number of lags needed (T <= h for consecutive origins), there is no test (statistic and p_value are NA, with a warning of class mt_warning_dm): lag 0 would ignore the correlation of overlapping test years and give too small p-values. For long horizons, use more origins or origins spaced h years apart. When the variance estimate with lags up to h - 1 is not positive, the test uses lag 0, as forecast::dm.test() does, with the same warning. The p-values are not adjusted for the number of tests (models, targets, horizons); see stats::p.adjust().

References

Diebold FX, Mariano RS (1995). Comparing predictive accuracy. Journal of Business & Economic Statistics 13(3): 253-263.

Harvey D, Leybourne S, Newbold P (1997). Testing the equality of prediction mean squared errors. International Journal of Forecasting 13(2): 281-291.

See also

mt_compare(), mt_score_table(), mt_score().

Examples

x <- mt_example(deaths = "single", years = 1990:2012)
bt <- mt_compare(list(rw = rwd(), lc = lee_carter()), x, origins = 2001:2007, h = 3, n_draws = 30)
mt_dm_test(bt)
#>     model    ref target metric horizon n_origins   lag      score  score_ref
#>    <char> <char> <char> <char>  <fctr>     <int> <int>      <num>      <num>
#> 1:     lc     rw   rate   crps       1         7     0 0.03573127 0.04750121
#> 2:     lc     rw   rate   crps       2         7     1 0.03613443 0.04969118
#> 3:     lc     rw   rate   crps       3         7     2 0.03729030 0.05588227
#> 4:     lc     rw   rate   crps     all         7     2 0.03638533 0.05102489
#>      mean_diff statistic      p_value
#>          <num>     <num>        <num>
#> 1: -0.01176994 -8.088596 0.0001913927
#> 2: -0.01355675 -6.981889 0.0004294763
#> 3: -0.01859197 -7.064353 0.0004029532
